idiom_name: remember { mutableStateOf(...) } (rememberSaveable where it must survive) in the smallest composable; plain private properties in the smallest class for view-system UIs
implementation_notes: Compose supplies the colocated cell directly: remember stores a value in the composition of the composable that declares it, mutableStateOf makes it observable (only composables that read it recompose), and rememberSaveable additionally survives configuration or process recreation. The replacement for the classic structure is this remembered cell: state starts in the composable that uses it, and hoisting - moving the value to the caller - is the documented deliberate exception, applied when a reusable composable must let a parent read or control the state. For view-system screens the same rule is expressed with a private property in the smallest owner (Activity/Fragment, ViewHolder, or a per-screen state holder), and state that must outlive the screen belongs in a ViewModel or other state holder rather than in the view.
pitfalls: remember is scoped to the composition: leaving and re-entering it (navigation, configuration change, a key change) discards the value; use rememberSaveable or a ViewModel where survival is required.
Hoisting state that no caller needs adds parameters and callbacks without benefit; remember is the colocated default and should be lifted only for a named external consumer.
Keys passed to remember/rememberSaveable reset the state whenever they change, and keys built from unstable values (new lambdas, freshly allocated objects) reset it on every recomposition.
